title: Schema diagnostics CLI and OpenAI-compat error mapping for strict response_format
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: customers reported opaque schema validation failures during streamed responses and limited debug signals when using the private deployment CLI. This PR adds an opt-in diagnostic flow and improves runtime error shapes for strict response_format. Motivations: make schema failures actionable, reduce support time, and preserve legacy OpenAI-compat semantics where required. Changes: 1) Introduce `redwoodctl schema-probe` to query a live host or a recorded stream and output a compact failure summary that contains an `error_code`, failing_path, token_preview (redacted by default), and a suggested_fix hint; 2) Enhance the runtime validator to attach a `user_hint` and a `retryability` tag to validation errors emitted during streaming so clients (SDKs/agents) can decide whether to resume, retry, or fallback; 3) Add an OpenAI-compat adapter that maps strict-mode validation errors to an `openai.error`-shaped payload when compatibility_flag is enabled so legacy clients see expected shapes; 4) Add e2e streaming tests covering resume after soft checkpoints and unit tests for redaction, error codes, and namespace enforcement; 5) Update docs and changelog with examples and recommended SDK behaviors. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in — strict behavior requires response_format to include strictness set to strict or explicit API flag. Rollout: internal early access, monitor schema_error_rate and support volume for 2 weeks. Follow-ups: expand schema-probe export to JSONL for telemetry (ENG-7421) and provide SDK helpers for retryability and resume tokens (ENG-7460).
